chains.title: T allele increases HOXB13 binding at an intronic RFX6 enhancer, raising RFX6 expression in AR-positive prostate epithelium
chains.element: Intronic enhancer of RFX6 at 6q22.1 containing the rs339331 TTTA/HOXB13-like core
chains.cell_type: Androgen-receptor-positive luminal prostate epithelial cells (LNCaP as model)

links.claim: The ref T allele restores a HOXB13 consensus core (TTA-containing homeodomain site) that is disrupted by the alt C, so HOXB13 binds the T allele more strongly; HOXB13 is the homeodomain TF chosen because it is the prostate-lineage-restricted member of the family highly expressed in LNCaP, whereas most other homeodomain TFs sharing this specificity group are not expressed there.

The variant lies in an intronic element of RFX6 that behaves as an androgen-responsive enhancer bound by HOXB13 and FOXA1 in prostate cells; the T allele gives higher enhancer activity in reporter assays.
The enhancer loops to and up-regulates RFX6, the nearest gene, making rs339331 an eQTL for RFX6 in prostate tissue with T as the higher-expression allele.
The effect is restricted to AR/HOXB13/FOXA1-positive luminal prostate epithelium, the cell of origin of prostate adenocarcinoma.
Elevated RFX6 promotes proliferation and invasive behaviour of prostate epithelial cells, increasing prostate cancer risk and aggressiveness for T carriers.

predictions: HOXB13 ChIP-seq in heterozygous prostate cells shows allelic imbalance favouring the T allele
HOXB13 knockdown abolishes the allelic difference in reporter activity and lowers RFX6
rs339331 is an RFX6 eQTL in prostate tissue with T as the high-expression allele
falsified_if: No HOXB13 occupancy at the locus by ChIP-seq, or no allelic imbalance in heterozygotes
HOXB13 knockdown leaves allele-specific enhancer activity unchanged

chains.title: Null: rs339331 has no TF-mediated allelic effect; the association is carried by a linked variant on the 6q22 haplotype
predictions: No allelic imbalance in any TF ChIP-seq or in ATAC at rs339331 in heterozygous prostate cells
Allele-swap (CRISPR knock-in) at rs339331 does not change RFX6 expression
Fine-mapping credible set keeps other variants with comparable posterior probability, and one of them shows the functional signal
falsified_if: CRISPR allele swap of rs339331 alone changes RFX6 expression or local chromatin accessibility
Reproducible allele-specific TF occupancy at the site in heterozygotes

chains.title: Allelic FOXA1 pioneer binding at the same element drives the RFX6 enhancer difference
chains.element: Same 6q22.1 intronic RFX6 enhancer, within a composite forkhead/homeodomain module

links.claim: The T allele improves a forkhead-like core (TGTTT/AAACA family motif) so FOXA1 binds more; FOXA1 is chosen among forkhead factors because it is the dominant, highly expressed forkhead pioneer factor in LNCaP and prostate luminal cells.
FOXA1 pioneering opens the chromatin of the element, and loss of the site on the C allele reduces accessibility and enhancer output.
Reduced accessibility lowers RFX6 transcription from the linked promoter.
FOXA1 dependence confines the effect to luminal prostate epithelium.
Allele-dependent RFX6 levels modulate prostate cancer susceptibility.

predictions: ATAC/DNase allelic imbalance at the element favouring T even after HOXB13 depletion
FOXA1 ChIP-seq allelic imbalance favouring T
FOXA1 knockdown, not HOXB13 knockdown, collapses the allelic difference
falsified_if: FOXA1 ChIP shows no allelic imbalance at rs339331
Allelic enhancer activity persists after FOXA1 depletion

chains.title: The alt C allele creates a repressive site for an RFX-family factor that dampens the element
chains.element: Same intronic element, with a C-dependent X-box-like half site

links.claim: The C allele generates a partial X-box (GTTRCC-like) recognised by RFX-family proteins; RFX6 is chosen within this specificity group because it is the family member expressed at the locus and in prostate tissue, giving a plausible local autoregulatory loop.
RFX binding on the C allele represses the enhancer or competes with homeodomain/forkhead occupancy.
Negative autoregulation lowers RFX6 expression specifically from the C haplotype.
Restricted to cells expressing RFX6, chiefly prostate epithelium and pancreatic/intestinal endocrine cells.
Lower RFX6 on C haplotypes is protective; T carriers retain higher RFX6 and higher risk.

predictions: RFX6 ChIP or motif-directed EMSA shows C-preferential binding
RFX6 knockdown raises reporter activity selectively for the C allele
falsified_if: No RFX-family occupancy at the element
C allele shows no gain of any protein complex in EMSA

matrix.test: HOXB13 ChIP-seq (or ChIP-qPCR with allele-specific readout) in rs339331-heterozygous prostate cells

outcomes.outcome: Little or no HOXB13 imbalance; signal may be weak and FOXA1-dependent

matrix.test: Luciferase reporter with T vs C element in LNCaP, with and without HOXB13 or FOXA1 knockdown

outcomes.outcome: T > C activity, difference lost on HOXB13 knockdown
T > C activity, difference lost on FOXA1 knockdown
C < T because C gains repression; difference lost on RFX6 knockdown

matrix.test: CRISPR allele swap of rs339331 in LNCaP and RFX6 qPCR

outcomes.outcome: T knock-in raises RFX6 and accessibility

matrix.test: Prostate-tissue eQTL lookup for RFX6 at rs339331

outcomes.outcome: eQTL absent or fully explained by linked variants

next_experiment: Reanalyse existing LNCaP HOXB13 ChIP-seq (and matched FOXA1 ChIP-seq) reads overlapping rs339331 in heterozygous cells for allele-specific occupancy: it is essentially free, and T-biased HOXB13 reads support H1 while balanced reads with T-biased FOXA1 support H2 (and no occupancy at all supports the null).
